title: Connecting authors of Basque documentary heritage on Wikipedia and Wikidata
content:
The programme “Connecting authors of Basque documentary heritage on Wikipedia and Wikidata”, launched by the Sancho el Sabio Vital Foundation and Wikimedia Spain, has promoted the dissemination of Basque documentary heritage through free knowledge, combining training, guidance and collaborative editing. 

Over the course of several months, the initiative has introduced Wikimedia tools to professionals and new audiences, with the aim of raising the profile of authors linked to Basque culture. 

In total, 43 people took part in the programme’s activities, which unfolded in different stages, from the initial training sessions to an edit-a-thon dedicated to putting the knowledge gained into practice. 

The various sessions featured Wikimedia Spain members with experience of the Wikimedia ecosystem and specialist knowledge of its projects and tools. Their contribution enabled the programme to cover everything from the principles of editing on Wikipedia to the potential of Wikidata for cultural institutions, combining technical knowledge and practical experience.

title: Documenting the Egungun Masorantan Festival in Igosun: Preserving Yoruba Living Heritage Through Community-Based Digital Documentation
content:
On Saturday, 22 August 2025, the African Institute for Heritage Intelligence (AIHI) in collaboration with Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa, documented the annual Egungun Masorantan Festival, also known as Egungun Onigosun, in Igosun, Oyun Local Government Area of Kwara State, Nigeria. The documentation team which was lead by Salako Lukman Olamilekan the documentation formed part of the Institute’s community heritage project, which seeks to preserve, document and improve access to African cultural heritage through digital technologies, open knowledge and community engagement.

The Egungun Masorantan is a distinctive traditional masquerade associated with the King of Igosun and represents an important expression of the town’s Yoruba cultural identity. Beyond its visual appearance and public performance, the masquerade embodies layers of indigenous knowledge, spirituality, oral history, traditional craftsmanship, music, ritual practices and community memory.

title: Language and Internationalization/Newsletters/12
content:
Welcome to the October 2026 edition of the Language and internationalization newsletter by the Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Language and Product Localization team! This newsletter provides you with quarterly updates on new feature developments, improvements in various language-related technical projects and support work, community meetings, and ideas to get involved in contributing to the projects.

Subscribe to the newsletter

translatewiki.net is a platform for gathering translations of interface messages for Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. This quarter, 16 new projects and MediaWiki extensions, including Link Count, Moderator Toolkit, and Recent Page Stats, were added to the platform. In addition, three languages, Khiamniungan Naga (kix), Tsishingini (tsw), and Izere (izr), were added to translatewiki.net, while Oostfräisk (frs) was added to MediaWiki’s language names configuration.[1] Volunteers also improved language support through updates to namespace translations and language fallback configuration for Magahi[2][3], and fixes to redirects for Sindhi Arabic.[4]

title: Connecting global knowledge with Wikimedia: International Partnerships at the Content Partnerships Hub
content:
International organisations hold a wealth of knowledge that can enrich Wikimedia projects, from resources on climate change and biodiversity to research on gender equality, human rights and public health. However, transforming this knowledge into freely accessible and reusable content requires more than simply making information available. It requires relationships, institutional understanding, technical expertise and collaboration with Wikimedia communities.

The International Partnerships programme of the Content Partnerships Hub, coordinated by Wikimedia Sverige, works to bridge these worlds. By connecting United Nations agencies, intergovernmental organisations and Wikimedia contributors, the programme helps institutions understand the opportunities offered by Wikimedia projects while supporting communities in accessing and reusing valuable institutional knowledge. This work includes developing institutional partnerships, facilitating the release of openly licensed content, supporting Wikimedians in Residence and creating resources that strengthen the capacity of individuals working between Wikimedia communities and partner organisations.

title: What India still reads: ten years of Indian-language Wikipedias, and the readers we are losing
content:
Ten years ago, Hindi Wikipedia had about 190 million human pageviews in a year. In the twelve months to October 2026 it had about 186 million. In between, it climbed past 670 million. Indian-language Wikipedias did not slowly grow over the last decade. They rose very fast, peaked in early 2024, and then lost more than half of their readers’ visits in under three years.

That is the story behind a question I took to WikiConference India 2026 in Kochi: what does India actually read on Wikipedia? I gave a five-minute lightning talk on it on 5 September 2026. Since then I have rechecked every number, widened the study from 27 to 29 languages, gone back ten years, and sorted the most-read articles into topics. This post is the full version: what India reads, what it has stopped reading, and what that means for all of us who write for these readers.

Wikimedia communities in India measure their work carefully. Campaign reports count articles created, photographs uploaded, participants trained and events held. Those numbers matter. They show what a programme set out to do and what it delivered.

title: Send us your squares! The Arpilleras art project at Wikimania 2027
content:
The central question of Wikimania 2027 is “What Internet do we want?”

In the lead-up to the event in Santiago, we are calling for answers from everyone in the Wikimedia movement. And rather than limiting answers to surveys, slides, and conference sessions, we are offering the possibility for community members to express their ideas about the Internet we want – artistically.

It doesn’t matter whether or not you are traveling to attend the event in person. To participate, all you have to do is to send us a fabric square – 20cm by 20cm, with a 3cm margin on each side – which will be woven into our collective tapestry.

The end product will be an arpillera – a massive patchwork art piece drawing on Chilean tradition. After the event, we will have a lasting historical record – both physical and digital – capturing the creativity and diversity of opinion across the Wikimedia movement.

title: EduWiki at LDC 2026: Can Wikimedia Education Reach Learners in Every Language?
content:
Language shapes who gets to participate in Wikimedia education. It influences whether educators can find useful learning materials, whether smaller language communities receive the support they need, and whether Wikimedia education programmes can be adapted to local contexts.

On 4 October 2026, Barakat Adegboye facilitated a workshop on behalf of EduWiki Hub at the Language Diversity Conference in Ghana. Titled Between Language and Access: Rethinking Wikimedia in Education for Underrepresented Languages, the session brought together 30 participants to explore these questions.

The session opened with a quick icebreaker. Participants were given a page from the Albanian translation of the EduWiki Newcomer’s Starter Kit and invited to look for specific words. It was a fun way to get everyone involved while introducing the idea that language can shape access to information and learning resources.

title: Creating Safer and Resilient Spaces: The Community Safety Toolkit by Wikimedia Deutschland
content:
For Wikimedia Deutschland (WMDE), community safety is not about having the perfect plan for when something goes wrong. It is about building the skills, knowledge and confidence to act before, during and after challenging situations. Over the past years, WMDE has worked with volunteers, communities and affiliates on questions around awareness, safety and psychosocial support. We wanted to make that experience easier to share and use.

The result is the WMDE Community Safety Toolkit: a collection of practical resources designed for chapters, affiliates and Wikimedia communities who want to make their own events and interactions safer in ways that fit their context, capacity and needs. The Toolkit was developed by WMDE’s Team Support & Consultancy. It is not an official Wikimedia Foundation standard: we share what works for us.

title: African Technical Needs Survey: Analysis & Findings
content: When we started planning the WikiIndaba Hackathon 2026, we wanted to think about how to make the event as useful as possible for participants. Beyond the usual hackathon experience, we wanted people to get hands-on support, work together and, most importantly, spend time improving tools that African Wikimedia communities actually need. We didn’t want to make assumptions about what those needs were, so we decided to ask the community. Wiki Mentor Africa (WMA), on behalf of the hackathon planning committee, put together a Technical Needs Survey to find out which tools people currently use, what challenges they face and what they’d like to see improved.

title: We need to talk about being a good neighbor
content: Summary: Wikimedians depend on the valuable work of journalists, cultural heritage institutions, photographers and many volunteer contributors. We are asking AI companies to provide better credit when they are using our work. We should lead by example, and reflect on how good we are at giving credit to partners in the knowledge ecosystem. Don’t do the minimum required but do as much as possible to help them thrive. I invite you to join the conversation.

title: Dagaare Wikimedians Celebrate Wikidata’s 14th Birthday in Ghana
content:
We celebrated, learn, had interesting conversations, laughter, photography and of course, a delicious birthday cake! We also meet an active community member for the first time in person and some other community members who join the celebration and had an opportunity to learn more about Wikidata.

The Dagaare Wikimedia Community brought people together to celebrate free knowledge, learn about Wikimedia projects and enjoy the spirits of community.

On 29th of October 2026, Dagaare Wikimedians came together to celebrate Wikidata’s 14th birthday. It was a great opportunity to learn, share experiences, meet new people and celebrate the important role that Wikidata plays in making knowledge freely accessible to everyone.

participants who join the celebration were taught how to create lexemes and Wikidata items by User Vision L1. This session were much focus on the lexemes, They learn to create lexemes, add statement, senses, and forms. You could see the joy in some participants faces after being able to create lexemes and adding statement like P13 and images to them. Link to dashboard, project page here.
